cards.title: One mirror reader for devices and sleep: single-flight, generation-checked
acceptance: mirror: read A is issued, a nudge issues read B, B resolves before A -> the applied state is B's answer and A's late answer is discarded (generation token minted at issue decides authority, not arrival order)

devices: a /devices read listing pending row P is out; the person answers P and the act's read (no P) resolves first; the first read resolves last -> view.pending has no P, seenAt has no P, and wizardStep(kind, branch, state, answered) stays 'done' (today P reappears with a fresh seenAt and Approve disarms)
devices: three bus frames (pair.requested, peer.changed, vitals.changed) land while one /devices read is out -> exactly 2 GET /devices in total (the one out, one after), never 4
devices: a bus reconnect within REREAD_MIN_MS of the last read -> no GET /devices; a reconnect at or after it -> exactly one (today every 15 s quiet-stream reconnect re-reads unconditionally)
devices: startDevices() twice, the first stop called -> still following (follows 1, stops 0); the second stop -> stops 1 (today the first stop ends the follow for both holders)
mirror: a read that rejects leaves no joinable flight -> the next load() issues a fresh GET and the store's problem sentence clears on its success
sleep (guard): the existing 'reads again on each sleep.changed, once more for one that lands mid-read, and on a reconnect at most every 5 s' passes unchanged on the shared reader
sleep (guard): the existing 'follows the bus once for any number of holders, and stops with the last' passes unchanged

cards.body:
## Summary
The two mirrors on the Mind depth read the daemon two different ways. Sleep has one read at a time, re-reads after a nudge that lands mid-read, throttles reconnects and counts its holders. Devices has none of that: four bus kinds, every reconnect, every act and a 30 s drawer timer each fire their own GET /devices, and whichever answer lands last wins. Lift the sleep discipline into one small reader (`lib/mirror.ts`) with a generation token, and put both stores on it.

## Description
`createMirror({ read, apply, onFail, now, rereadMinMs, maxRepeats })` returns `load()`, `nudge()`, `reconnected()` and `hold()`. `load()` joins the flight that is out. A nudge during a flight marks it dirty, and the reader re-issues once the flight settles. Each flight mints a generation at issue and `apply` runs only while that generation is current, so a slow answer issued before a change can never overwrite a newer one (realtime-events/push-vs-refetch-reconciliation: generation tokens; client-fetch-cache/in-flight-dedup: register before suspend, remove on both settle paths). `reconnected()` throttles to `rereadMinMs`. `hold()` counts holders and starts and stops the bus follow. Devices: `DevicesDeps.follow` gains the `onConnected` argument sleep already has, `load`/`act` go through the reader, and `startDevices` becomes counted. Sleep: its module globals (`reading`, `nudgesSinceRead`, `lastRead`, `holders`, `unfollow`) are replaced by one reader with its behaviour unchanged, pinned by its two existing tests.

## Flow
- bus frame / act settle / drawer tick -> mirror.nudge() or load() -> at most one GET out, plus one dirty re-read after it
- reconnect -> mirror.reconnected() -> a read only if rereadMinMs has passed
- an answer whose generation is stale -> dropped; the state never steps back

## Expected impact
A whole class of defects closes: a revoked peer, an answered request or an old room word can no longer come back from a read that was already stale when it was issued. Wizard flicker from Done back to Approve, and Approve re-disarming, both go. GET /devices traffic while the level is open falls from one read per frame plus one per 15 s reconnect to at most two per burst. The next mirror (tasks, connectors) gets the reader for free.

## Evaluation
Claim: the devices mirror can no longer apply an answer older than one it already applied, and both mirrors share one read discipline.
Before: 0 of 6 non-guard acceptance cases pass (cases 1-6); the 2 guards pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases (vitest, a fake fetch whose responses resolve out of order)
Result: better
Gate: none

cards.title: Answer her proposals in one pass: staged forgets, Keep all, and a 6 s Undo
shared_surfaces: r4 core-sleep-and-vitals card B also edits scenes/mind/sleep.tsx and sleep.test.tsx (the coordinator sequences)
acceptance: store: stage(proposalId, 'forget') -> no POST /sleep/proposals/<id> before COMMIT_MS; the proposal is listed in staged and left out of the open list the section draws; after COMMIT_MS exactly one POST with {action:'forget', node_id:null}
store: stage then undo() inside the window -> no POST is ever sent, and the proposal is drawn open again with no error

store: stageAll('keep') over 3 open forget proposals and 1 contradiction -> the 3 forgets are staged as one batch with one Undo; the contradiction is not staged (it needs a choice); after COMMIT_MS, 3 POSTs with at most 2 in flight at once
store: a sleep.changed re-read lands mid-window and still lists the staged ids as open -> they stay out of the drawn open list until the batch commits or is undone (freeze-refresh-during-window)
store: the last holder stops (the section unmounts) while a batch is staged -> the batch commits at once, not dropped (flush-on-teardown)
store: a second stage while a batch is pending -> the pending batch commits first, then the new one opens its own window (single-pending-batch-invariant), so one Undo never covers two decisions
store: 1 of 3 committed POSTs is refused (409) -> that proposal comes back open with its refusal under it; the other 2 are gone after the read that follows
section: with a batch staged, the 'Waiting for you' block shows 'Forgetting 3 · Undo' with the seconds left, and pressing Undo calls actions.undo()

apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/sleep.tsx:356 - a forget proposal's Forget is one press straight to the POST, beside Keep in the same row
apps/desktop/src/scenes/mind/sleep.tsx:291 - proposals are answered one row at a time; there is no bulk mode

cards.body:
## Summary
A sleep can leave up to 20 open proposals, and each one is answered by its own press. A Forget is final the moment it is pressed: the memory is retired and the proposal closed in one call, with no route back. Make the block a queue a person can clear in one pass. Keep all, or Forget, stages the decision for a short window with one Undo that says what it will do and how long is left, then commits as a bounded batch.

## Description
The store gains `staged: { ids, action, nodeIds, until } | null`, `stage(id, action, nodeId?)`, `stageAll('keep' | 'forget')` (forget proposals only: a contradiction always asks which memory goes, and is never bulk-forgotten), `undo()` and `commitNow()`. One timer is armed per batch (`COMMIT_MS` = 6000). The section draws the open list minus the staged ids, so a re-read cannot repaint them back mid-window. Commit fans out with at most 2 in flight and runs one read after it. A refused row comes back open with its sentence under it. Stopping the last holder flushes a staged batch rather than dropping it: the person decided, and leaving the section is not a cancel. These are the batch-undo-commit-window techniques deferred-write-window, single-pending-batch-invariant, freeze-refresh-during-window, flush-on-teardown, bounded-fanout-commit and partial-failure-reselect. The decision stays the person's alone: nothing is sent that was not pressed, and the window only adds a way back.

## Flow
- Forget on a row, or Keep all -> rows leave the list, the bar reads 'Forgetting 1 · Undo (6 s)'
- Undo -> rows return, nothing was sent
- the window ends, or the section closes -> POSTs (2 at a time) -> one re-read -> refused rows come back with their reason

## Expected impact
A mis-pressed Forget, today a retired memory, can be taken back for 6 seconds. Clearing a full queue of 20 takes 2 presses instead of 20, so her proposal cap stops silently dropping new offers. The person sees the outcome before it is final rather than after.

## Evaluation
Claim: forget and keep decisions are deferred behind one Undo, can be applied to the queue at once, and are never lost or resurrected by a refresh.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - the acceptance cases (vitest fake timers plus the store's fake fetch; the section rendered on a fixture model)
Result: better
Gate: none

rehomed: A proposal shows both memories' words, not two raw node ids - void here: it is r4 core-sleep-and-vitals card B.
The message box warns before sending to an asleep or full computer (presence and held are already in the mirror) - S; it is slot B's runner-up.
Each proposal says when it lapses (created_at + 14 d) and that lapsing forgets nothing - S, and the client would have to mirror PROPOSAL_EXPIRE_D.
The pending card could name the requester's private-network address against the overlay list - needs a daemon PendingView field (peer-devices context), not this one.
Auto-renewing an expired pairing window while the wizard is open - it mints more credentials than a person asked for; a policy call, not a card.
